reasons: Section 22.1 as drafted permits audits 'at any time without notice' with remote access to Customer systems — squarely in the rule's walk-away territory and failing the fallback on frequency, notice and system access, so 'deviation' is the correct classification.

The redline reaches the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, business hours, off-site independent auditor bound by confidentiality, no remote/direct system access) while leaving the already-compliant cost allocation in § 22.2 untouched — no over-flagging of acceptable terms.

The failed 'minimal edit' heuristic (0.798 changed-character ratio) is acceptable here: the original sentence grants unlimited, unannounced audits plus remote access, so the limits cannot be inserted without rewriting the sentence; no extraneous obligations were added.
Comment is accurate, concise, in the required voice and prefix, cites the playbook position, notes consistency with § 22.2's existing bar on direct system access, and offers the 15-day fallback.
